newsitem.title: ITALY: Brazil to launch debut 20-yr 500 bln lire bond-DMG.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to launch debut 20-yr 500 bln lire bond-DMG.

text.p: The Federative Republic of Brazil will soon launch its first Eurolira bond and plans a 500 billion lire offering with a 20-year maturity.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG), which with representatives of the Brazilian government presented the mooted deal to investors in Milan on Thursday, will be the lead manager.

"The bond could be launched as early as next Monday, possibly at mid-week, depending on market turbulence after the the second and final round of the French elections (on Sunday)", a DMG official said.
The plain vanilla bond will have a coupon of around 11 percent. Moody's and Standard & Poor's rate Brazil's foreign currency debt B1 and BB- respectively.
Brazil wants to lengthen the duration of its debt. This issue will set a benchmark in the lira sector and will help diversify Brazil's external funding sources.
This week Brazil announced it would issue at least $1 billion of 30-year global bonds which may be exchanged for Brady bonds or cash.

The lira bond's terms will be in line with the United States of Mexico's 20-year lira issue which also pays an 11 percent coupon. The Mexico issue, for 500 billion lire, was launched at a price of 99.30 ex-full fees and at 1330 GMT on Thursday was trading at 100.00 after closing on Wednesday at 99.875.
In January, Brazilian state bank BNDES launched a five-year bond for 500 billion lire with an 8.5 percent coupon.
In 1996, telecommunications company Telebras launched a three-year, 500 billion lire bond carrying a 13 percent coupon.
